It was founded by Dennis Rushen and David Hayle in 2002 and relaunched by [[Oliver Oakes]] in 2015.{{cite news|url=http://www.hitechracing.net/index.php?categoryid=10 |title=Hitech Racing 2007 Champions |work=hitechracing.net |publisher=[[Hitech Racing]] |access-date=28 January 2021 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514234409/http://www.hitechracing.net/index.php?categoryid=10 |archive-date=May 14, 2008 }} Currently, Hitech competes in [[FIA Formula 2 Championship|FIA Formula 2]], [[FIA Formula 3 Championship|FIA Formula 3]],[[Formula Regional Oceania Trophy]], [[Eurocup-3]], [[GB3 Championship]], [[F4 British Championship|British F4]], [[F1 Academy]], [[Formula 4 UAE Championship#Formula Trophy UAE|Formula Trophy UAE]] and [[UAE4 Series]]. The team also supports Toyota drivers in [[Super Formula Championship]]. == History == === Hitech Racing (2002–2014) === Hitech Racing started out in the [[British Formula 3 Championship]] in 2003. The team also competed in the South American Formula Three Series, namely the [[Formula 3 Sudamericana]].{{Cite web |title=Hitech Racing Brazil |url=http://www.hitechracing.com.br/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140503222217/http://www.hitechracing.com.br/ |archive-date=3 May 2014 |access-date=3 May 2014}} In its first season, Hitech scored five [[pole position]]s and six podium finishes, with drivers [[Danny Watts]] and [[Eric Salignon]]. Andrew Thompson also contributed some points finishes. Watts finished the British F3 Championship in 5th place in a season that included a memorable win at [[Castle Combe Circuit|Castle Combe]]. In the [[Korea Super Prix]], guest driver [[Richard Antinucci]] achieved Hitech's first international race win. In the second season, 2004, Thompson was retained and joined by drivers [[Marko Asmer]], [[James Walker (racing driver)|James Walker]], and [[Lucas di Grassi|Lucas Di Grassi]]. Di Grassi had two wins and was classified in eighth place overall. Another of that year's highlights was a podium finish on Di Grassi's début at the [[Macau Grand Prix]]. Asmer managed to finish the championship closing the top 10. In 2005, Hitech retained Asmer and brought in [[Tim Bridgman]] from [[Formula BMW]]. Asmer was the best of the duo, scoring no less than five second places, but missing out on an actual win, even so managing to snatch the fourth place in the championship. For 2006, Hitech brought back James Walker, alongside [[James Jakes]] and [[Salvador Durán]], with Jakes finishing 8th, Walker 9th and Durán 10th in a poor season that only heralded one podium finish (achieved by Walker). In 2007 Hitech retained the services of Marko Asmer who joined Austrian Walter Grubmuller for an assault on the British F3 Championship. Hitech and Asmer took the title, scoring 11 poles, 11 wins (from 22 races) and 9 fastest laps. Marko Asmer secured the title long before the final round and in the end by a margin of 85 points from [[Maro Engel]]. In 2008, [[Walter Grubmüller|Walter Grubmuller]] was joined by the youngest driver in the sport, [[Max Chilton]].{{cite web|url=https://www.autosport.com/f3/news/64583/hitech-sign-max-chilton-for-2008|title=Hitech sign Max Chilton for 2008|last=Freeman|first=Glenn|date=9 January 2008|website=Autosport.com|language=en|access-date=28 January 2021}} For 2012, Brazilian [[Felipe Guimarães]] took 4 wins and two poles to end fourth with Hitech Racing Brazil in the [[Formula Three Sudamericana]] series. In 2013, Hitech's Brazilian ace [[Felipe Guimarães]] took both the [[Formula 3 Brazil Open]] and the [[Formula Three Sudamericana]] series titles, winning 13 races and obtaining 7 poles and 12 fastest laps in the process. In 2014, Brazilian [[Felipe Guimarães]] defended his [[Formula 3 Brazil Open]] title with Hitech Racing Brazil in January 2014 at the [[2014 Formula 3 Brazil Open]] with his teammate [[Victor Hitech GP also supplied race engineers and pit crew for each of the cars.{{Cite web|url=https://racer.com/2018/12/12/hitech-gp-to-operate-w-series-2019-operations/|title=Hitech GP to operate W Series' 2019 operations|date=12 December 2018|website=RACER|language=en|access-date=2019-09-16}} This partnership was discontinued for the [[2021 W Series|2021 season]] following the [[2020 W Series|2020 season's]] cancellation due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and Hitech GP's subsequent expansion into other series.{{Cite web|url=https://formulascout.com/hitech-confirms-discontinuation-of-w-series-involvement-for-2021/71037/|title=Hitech confirms discontinuation of W Series involvement for 2021|last=Wood|first=Elliot|date=14 November 2020|website=Formula Scout|language=en|access-date=28 January 2021}} For the inaugural [[2019 FIA Motorsport Games Formula 4 Cup ]] all drivers utilized [[KC Motorgroup|KCMG]] KC MG-01 cars, which were operated by Hitech GP. 2002 by Dennis Rushen and David Hayle as HiTech Racing Ltd. In 2015 Hayle, in partnership with [[Oliver Oakes]], formed the company and its assets into a new company, Hitech Grand Prix Ltd, to compete in the [[FIA Formula 3 European Championship]]. In 2016, Hitech joined forces with [[ART Grand Prix]] to complete a full season in the FIA F3 European Championship. Gaining [[Nikita Mazepin]] as a driver, they also gained Russian minerals company [[Uralkali]] as a sponsor, and partial ownership by [[Dmitry Mazepin]]. Over the next few years, Mazepin increased his holding through [[Cyprus]]-based investment company Bergton Management Ltd to 75%. In March 2022, following the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian war against Ukraine]], the shares held by Bergton Management Ltd were relinquished to Oakes, who took full control of the company.{{cite web|url=https://formulascout.com/hitech-gp-team-boss-oliver-oakes-takes-back-full-ownership-of-outfit/90178|title=Hitech GP team boss Oliver Oakes takes back full ownership of outfit|author=Ida Wood|publisher=Formula Scout|date=1 March 2022|accessdate=1 March 2023}} Oakes had formed a new company, Hitech Global Holdings Ltd, on 11 March 2022 to take control of the shares. This company was formed just three days after Mazepin and his son were sanctioned by both the UK Government and the [[European Union]], resulting in questions being asked in the UK Parliament over the effect of sanctions against Russia.{{cite web|url=https://www.theyworkforyou.com/pbc/2022-23/Economic_Crime_and_Corporate_Transparency_Bill/10-0_2022-11-08a.348.3|title=Clause 88 - Analysis of information for the purposes of crime prevention or detection|publisher=They Work For You|date=8 November 2022|accessdate=1 March 2023}} In May 2025, Oakes' brother William, a director at Hitech, was arrested near [[Silverstone Park]] charged with "transferring criminal property" and being found with "a large amount of cash".{{cite web |last1=Cary |first1=Tom |last2=Rumsby |first2=Ben |date=8 May 2025 |title=Revealed: Oliver Oakes resigned days after brother arrested near with 'large amount of cash' |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/formula-1/2025/05/08/oliver-oakes-alpine-resigned-days-police-raid-silverstone/ |website=telegraph.co.uk |publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |url-access=subscription|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508165539/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/formula-1/2025/05/08/oliver-oakes-alpine-resigned-days-police-raid-silverstone/ |archive-date=8 May 2025 |access-date=9 May 2025}} William resigned from his position shortly after and, in October 2025, Oliver Oakes transferred his voting and sharing powers to Chinese investor Guocai Liu.{{cite web|url=https://formulascout.com/oakes-cedes-control-at-hitech-gp-as-chinese-investor-takes-over/135352|title=Oakes cedes control at Hitech GP as Chinese investor takes over|website=Formula Scout|last=Wood|first=Ida|date=17 October 2025|access-date=19 February 2026}} == Current series results == === FIA Formula 2 Championship === {|class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; font-size:85%" |- ! extract: Hitech Grand Prix (formerly Hitech Racing) is a British motor racing team. It was founded by Dennis Rushen and David Hayle in 2002 and relaunched by Oliver Oakes in 2015. Currently, Hitech competes in FIA Formula 2, FIA Formula 3,Formula Regional Oceania Trophy, Eurocup-3, GB3 Championship, British F4, F1 Academy, Formula Trophy UAE and UAE4 Series. The team also supports Toyota drivers in Super Formula Championship.
